THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

Petitioner has preferred this petition under Section 407 of Cr.P.C. seeking transfer of C.C.No.1596/2014 pending on the file of JMFC, V Court, Mangaluru, Dakshina Kannada, to the Court of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Mangaluru for simultaneous trial and disposal with C.C.No.25/2016.

sentences.text: It is contended by the learned counsel for petitioner that in both the cases, the parties are one and the same and the allegations are identical in nature and the cause of action is also same.
He contends that if separate trials are held the same will prejudice the defense of the petitioner.

3. The proceedings in C.C.No.1596/2014 was initiated against the petitioner on the file of the JMFC,
V Court Mangaluru, Dakshina Kannada on a private complaint filed by respondent alleging an offence under Section 138 of the NI Act, in respect of dishonour of a cheque alleged to have been issued by the petitioner to the respondent for a sum of Rs.1,49,74,502/-.

sentences.text: 4. Application filed by the petitioner under Section 408 of Cr.P.C, has been rejected by the learned Sessions Judge in NC: 2023:KHC:41300 Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.182/2022 by order dated 17.08.2022.
The learned counsel for petitioner has relied on a judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sudhir and others V/s. State of M.P. reported in (2001) 2 SCC 688.

entities.text: Sudhir and others V/s. State of M.P. reported in (2001) 2 SCC 688
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The facts of the said case are entirely different and not applicable to the facts of the present case.
In the said case, facts are that there was a case and counter case wherein, one trial was pending before the learned Sessions Court and one before the learned Magistrate.

In that context, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the Sessions Court has power to try any offence under IPC and it is not necessary for the Sessions Court that the offence should be one exclusively triable by a Court of Session.

Hence, it was observed in the said case that the learned Sessions Judge ought not to have transferred the second case to the Chief Jurisdictional Magistrate, but he himself ought to have tried it in the manner indicated in Nathi Lal V/s. State of U.P. [1990 SCC (Cri) 638].
5.

entities.text: Nathi Lal V/s. State of U.P. [1990 SCC (Cri) 638]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand the parties may be one and the same but one case is registered against the accused inrespect of Section 138 of the NI Act and another inrespect of offences under the penal code.

Petitioner is the only accused in the NC: 2023:KHC:41300 proceedings initiated under Section 138 of NI Act, whereas inrespect of the case registered in crime No.210/2014 of Mangaluru North Police Station, there are 7 accused in the FIR and the charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner and one more accused i.e., respondent No.2 herein.

The allegations are that, the petitioner while working as Account Manager in the complainant's organization has misappropriated a huge amount and in this connection issued a cheque for Rs.1,49,74,502/- which when presented got dishonoured for insufficient funds in his account.
In the criminal case, it is alleged that the petitioner has misappropriated the funds for his personal use and made investments elsewhere.
6. The learned Sessions Judge while dismissing the application filed under Section 408 of Cr.P.C.
has rightly observed that the nature of both the cases are different and one is a summons proceedings and another is warrant proceedings and both cases have to be tried separately.

It is also observed that the defense of the petitioner in both the cases may be similar, but it will not affect the case of the petitioner, if they are tried separately and the question of prejudice will not arise.
NC: 2023:KHC:41300 7.
There is no error or illegality in the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge.
Hence, there is no merit in this petition.
8. Accordingly, petition is dismissed.
